intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Walk among the treetops on a network of hanging bridges suspended above the rainforest floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided or guided eco-walk offers incredible biodiversity including morpho butterflies, coatis, and resplendent quetzals, with stunning volcano views on clear days.
experiences.location: La Fortuna, Arenal Volcano National Park

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Wildlife & Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most beloved national park where lush rainforest meets pristine Pacific beaches. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, and scarlet macaws on well-marked trails before relaxing on the stunning Playa Manuel Antonio. A certified naturalist guide maximizes wildlife encounters.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biodiverse places on a guided trek through Corcovado's primary rainforest. Encounter tapirs, peccaries, scarlet macaws, and if lucky, the elusive jaguar. This raw, off-the-beaten-path experience is the pinnacle of eco-adventure in Central America.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shared shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport — look for a Soda (local Costa Rican diner) inside the terminal offering rice and beans dishes for around $5–8 USD before heading to the resort.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle in advance to save money (approx. $15–25 USD vs. $60+ for a private taxi). Have your resort address printed or saved offline. Exchange a small amount of USD to CRC (Costa Rican Colones) at the airport for tips and small purchases. February is dry season — expect warm, sunny weather.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, explore the immediate beachfront area around Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a long walk along the beach, watch wildlife such as pelicans, frigate birds, and possibly howler monkeys in nearby trees. Collect your bearings and orient yourself to the local area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local town on foot or by cheap local bus. Explore the central market, browse local sodas, and pick up any budget supplies (sunscreen, insect repellent, reusable water bottle) at a local farmacia or mini-super. Stroll through the town square and observe daily Costa Rican life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront for a stunning Pacific or Caribbean sunset (depending on resort location). Sit on the beach, relax, and enjoy the natural soundscape. Have dinner at a local soda near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Casado breakfast at a local soda near the resort — rice, beans, eggs, and fresh fruit juice for around $4–6 USD. Alternatively, grab fruit from a street vendor.
meals.lunch: Gallo pinto (rice and beans) with tortillas from a local market food stall — budget $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Soda dinner: Arroz con pollo (rice with chicken) or fresh fish casado at a local budget restaurant — $6–9 USD including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to allow recovery from travel. Use this day to plan upcoming activities, download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline), and ask resort staff for free local tips and discount activity recommendations. Stay hydrated — Costa Rica can be humid and warm in February.

day_by_day.morning: Head out early for a self-guided wildlife hike in a nearby national park or wildlife refuge accessible from the resort area. Look for iconic Costa Rican wildlife including sloths, iguanas, coatis, and tropical birds like toucans and scarlet macaws. Bring water, snacks, and a camera. Entry fees for national parks are typically $18 USD for foreigners — worth every cent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the park trails in the afternoon or return to the resort and rent a kayak or paddleboard from a local beach vendor (approx. $10–15/hour). Paddle along the coastline and look for marine wildlife including dolphins, sea turtles, and tropical fish in the shallows.
day_by_day.evening: Watch for bioluminescent plankton in the water at night if conditions are right (ask locals). Relax on the beach and stargaze — Costa Rica's skies are stunning with low light pollution outside of cities.

meals.breakfast: Pack a budget breakfast from the local market the night before — fresh bread, bananas, and a thermos of coffee to enjoy on the trail. Cost: $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch to take into the park — rice and beans in a container, fresh fruit, and water. Buy from a local soda the morning before. Cost: $3–4 USD.
meals.dinner: Beachside dinner at a casual open-air restaurant. Try ceviche de mariscos (fresh seafood ceviche) — a Costa Rican coastal staple. Budget $8–12 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy, closed-toe shoes for hiking. Apply insect repellent before entering forested areas. Bring a lightweight rain jacket even in dry season — afternoon showers can occur. Check park opening hours in advance (most open at 8am). Hiring a local guide for half a day ($20–30 USD) can dramatically improve wildlife spotting success.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget shared shuttle or local bus to the nearest zip-lining operation in the region (book in advance online for discounts). Most zip-line tours in Costa Rica run 2–3 hours and include multiple cables through the rainforest canopy. Prices range from $45–70 USD — look for combo deals or group discounts. This is a must-do eco-adventure experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole recommended by the tour operator. Many zip-line companies are located near rivers and waterfalls accessible with a short hike. Cool off with a refreshing swim in natural fresh water surrounded by jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by shared shuttle. Visit a local tienda (small grocery store) to stock up on budget snacks and drinks. Spend the evening on the beach or at the resort common area connecting with other budget travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda before departure — gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh juice. Budget $4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: Many zip-line operators are located near small towns with local sodas. Enjoy a filling casado lunch for $6–8 USD after your tour.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from the local tienda if your accommodation has kitchen access, or eat at a budget soda. Rice, beans, and fresh vegetables — $3–5 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining at least 1–2 days in advance, especially during peak February season. Wear comfortable, athletic clothing and closed-toe shoes. Secure loose items (glasses, hats, jewelry) before boarding zip cables. Weight and age restrictions may apply — check in advance. Combo packages (zip-line + rappelling + hanging bridges) offer better value.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for an early morning wildlife watching session on the beach or in nearby mangroves. February is an excellent time to spot nesting sea turtles (depending on beach location), shore birds, and early-rising howler monkeys. Bring binoculars if available. This is a completely free activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a free or low-cost community walking tour of the nearest town or village. Many destinations in Costa Rica offer volunteer-led tours. Alternatively, rent a bicycle from a local shop ($8–12/day) and explore the surrounding countryside, visiting local farms, viewpoints, and hidden beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural event, market, or festival if available (February often has local fiestas). Enjoy live music, traditional dance, and authentic street food. Ask resort staff about upcoming local events.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit smoothie and a pastry from a local bakery (panadería). Budget $3–4 USD.
meals.lunch: Street food from a local market — empanadas, tamales, or patacones (fried plantains with toppings). Budget $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Try a traditional Costa Rican olla de carne (beef and vegetable stew) at a local family-run soda. Budget $7–9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Early morning (5:30–7:30am) is the best time for wildlife observation — animals are most active at dawn. Bring a red-light flashlight for pre-dawn beach walks to avoid disturbing nesting sea turtles. Community-based tourism initiatives support local families and are often more affordable than commercial tours.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip via shared shuttle or local bus to a nearby national park or biological reserve not yet visited. Costa Rica's network of protected areas is world-class — options may include Manuel Antonio, Carara, Tortuguero, or Corcovado depending on resort location. Spend the morning on guided or self-guided trail walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, Jesus Christ lizards (basilisks), and hundreds of bird species. Swim at a protected park beach if available — some of Costa Rica's most pristine beaches are inside national parks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a sunset yoga session on the beach (many resorts and local instructors offer free or donation-based community classes). Reflect on the day's wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from the previous evening's market run — fresh fruit, granola bars, and water for the journey.
meals.lunch: Picnic inside the national park using packed food from a local soda or market. Budget $4–6 USD.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a nicer local restaurant for a celebratory mid-trip dinner. Try fresh grilled fish (pargo or tilapia) with rice, beans, and salad. Budget $12–15 USD.

day_by_day.notes: National park entry is $18 USD per person for international visitors. Arrive early as parks have daily visitor limits (especially Manuel Antonio). Wear reef-safe sunscreen for any beach swimming. Keep all food sealed in bags to avoid attracting wildlife — feeding animals is illegal and harmful. Download the iNaturalist app to help identify species.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the resort. Take advantage of the beachfront location — swim, snorkel in the shallows, or simply relax. This mid-trip rest day is important for energy management on a budget adventure trip. Do laundry at a local lavandería (laundry service) for $3–5 USD per load.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a free or inexpensive local cooking class or food tour. Many communities near tourist areas offer authentic Costa Rican cooking experiences where you learn to make gallo pinto, plantain dishes, and traditional desserts. Alternatively, visit a local chocolate or coffee farm for a $10–15 USD educational tour.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the resort's beachfront area after dark with a flashlight for nocturnal wildlife spotting — look for crabs, frogs, geckos, and insects. Night walks reveal a completely different ecosystem.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — fresh Costa Rican coffee, toast with natilla (sour cream), and fresh fruit. Budget $4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: If doing a cooking class, you'll likely eat what you prepare. Otherwise, enjoy a light lunch of ceviche and patacones at a beachside shack. Budget $5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Simple and satisfying: buy fresh ingredients from a local market and prepare a meal if kitchen facilities are available, or enjoy a budget soda dinner. Budget $4–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a strategic rest day. Use this time to review your remaining budget, plan the second half of your trip, and book any remaining activities in advance. Check in with family or friends back home. Recharge power banks and camera batteries. Reorganize your pack and do any necessary gear maintenance.

day_by_day.morning: Arrange a budget boat tour or water taxi to explore nearby mangrove estuaries, river deltas, or offshore islands. Mangrove tours are exceptional for wildlife — expect to see crocodiles, caimans, river otters, kingfishers, herons, and monkeys. Group tours typically cost $25–40 USD per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: If near a river, try white-water rafting on a beginner-friendly section (Class II–III rapids). Budget operators offer half-day trips for $45–65 USD including equipment and guide. This combines eco-adventure with an adrenaline rush through pristine jungle scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a well-deserved rest. Visit a local pulpería (corner store) for cold drinks and snacks. Share stories with fellow travelers at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early and energizing breakfast before water activities — eggs, gallo pinto, and fresh juice at a local soda. Budget $5–7 USD.
meals.lunch: Many rafting and boat tour operators include a simple lunch. If not, stop at a riverside or waterfront soda for fresh fish or chicken. Budget $6–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a beachfront soda or food cart. Try arroz con camarones (shrimp rice) if near the coast. Budget $7–10 USD.

day_by_day.notes: For rafting, wear clothes you don't mind getting completely wet. Waterproof dry bags for cameras and phones are essential — many operators provide these. Mangrove tours are best done at low tide for maximum wildlife visibility. Always use a licensed operator with safety equipment. Check operator reviews on TripAdvisor or Lonely Planet Thorn Tree forums.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer day trip via shared shuttle to a different region of Costa Rica not yet explored. Options depending on location include the Monteverde Cloud Forest, Arenal Volcano area, or the Osa Peninsula. Shared shuttles between major tourist hubs cost $15–35 USD each way. Spend the morning traveling and arriving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore your day-trip destination. If visiting Monteverde, walk the famous hanging bridges through cloud forest ($25–30 USD). If near Arenal, visit the free viewpoints of the volcano and hike lava field trails in the national park. If near Osa, explore pristine rainforest with exceptional biodiversity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort via shared shuttle in the late afternoon or evening. Alternatively, consider an overnight stay at a budget hostel in the day-trip area to save on return transport ($10–15 USD/night in a dorm).

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go breakfast before early shuttle departure — fruit, yogurt, and coffee from a local bakery. Budget $3–4 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local soda in your day-trip destination — try regional specialties. Budget $6–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at destination or upon return to resort area. Casado with local protein of the region. Budget $7–10 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Day trips to Monteverde or Arenal are long (3–5 hours each way from some coastal locations). Consider whether an overnight stay makes more logistical and financial sense than two round-trip shuttles. Book shuttles in advance during peak February season. Bring a light jacket — cloud forests and higher elevations can be cool even in dry season.

day_by_day.morning: Participate in a volunteer wildlife conservation activity if available in the area. Many organizations near popular tourist destinations offer half-day or full-day volunteer experiences such as sea turtle monitoring, reforestation planting, or wildlife rescue center assistance. Some are free; others charge a small contribution ($10–20 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture project for a self-guided or guided tour. Learn about sustainable agriculture, tropical fruit cultivation, and Costa Rica's commitment to environmental conservation. Many farms offer free or low-cost tours with advance arrangement.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free ranger talk or environmental education session if available at a nearby park visitor center. These sessions provide fascinating insights into Costa Rica's biodiversity and conservation success story.

meals.breakfast: Farm-fresh breakfast if volunteering at an agricultural project, or a simple soda breakfast near the resort. Budget $4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: Many volunteer organizations and farms provide simple lunches as part of the experience. If not, local soda lunch. Budget $5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner as a reward for giving back — try a restaurant with locally sourced ingredients supporting sustainable food systems. Budget $10–14 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Research volunteer opportunities in advance through reputable organizations like Volunteer World, Workaway, or directly through national park foundations. Avoid 'voluntourism' operations that charge excessive fees with unclear conservation outcomes. Genuine volunteer experiences are among the most rewarding and memorable parts of eco-travel in Costa Rica.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird watching walk — hire a local birding guide for 2–3 hours ($20–30 USD). Costa Rica has over 900 bird species and is considered one of the world's top birding destinations. February is excellent for spotting resident and migratory species. Target species may include resplendent quetzal, scarlet macaw, toucan, motmot, and hummingbirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby waterfall accessible by a moderate hike. Many of Costa Rica's most spectacular waterfalls are free or charge minimal entry fees ($2–5 USD). Swim in the natural pool at the base of the falls — a quintessential Costa Rican experience. Bring a dry bag for electronics.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk followed by a final exploration of the local restaurant scene. Try a new dish you haven't yet sampled during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Pre-birding light breakfast — coffee and a pastry to avoid noise from eating on the trail. Budget $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Post-waterfall lunch at a local soda or roadside restaurant near the trail. Fresh tropical fruit plate and a main dish. Budget $6–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Try traditional Costa Rican chifrijo (rice, beans, pork, pico de gallo, and avocado) at a local bar-restaurant. Budget $7–10 USD including a local Imperial beer.

day_by_day.notes: Birding is best done in the first 2 hours after sunrise when birds are most active. A good field guide app like Merlin Bird ID (free from Cornell Lab) dramatically enhances the experience. Waterfall hikes can be slippery — wear shoes with good grip. Check water quality before swimming in waterfall pools — avoid swimming near agricultural areas.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure: Book a combination eco-tour that packages multiple activities for better value. Options include a canopy + rappelling + river tubing combo, or a wildlife safari float + horseback riding package. These combination tours typically offer 15–25% savings versus booking individually. Prices range $60–90 USD for full-day combos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the combo tour or, if finished by midday, spend the afternoon at a local artisan market shopping for budget-friendly souvenirs. Look for handmade items by local artisans — carved wood, handmade jewelry, coffee, chocolate, and traditional pottery make excellent affordable gifts. Avoid airport souvenir shops which charge 2–3x more.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant discovered during the trip. Reflect on the journey, review photos, and begin packing for departure. Share a meal with fellow travelers you've met along the way.

meals.breakfast: Energizing breakfast before the big combo tour — full casado breakfast with protein and carbs. Budget $5–7 USD.
meals.lunch: Tour operator may include lunch, or stop at a local soda mid-tour. Budget $6–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Memorable farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a restaurant with ambiance. Try a whole fresh fish or lobster if near the coast (often surprisingly affordable at local spots). Budget $15–20 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon market visit to complete all souvenir shopping before the airport rush. Costa Rican coffee (Café Britt, Volio, or local cooperative brands) makes an excellent, lightweight, and affordable gift. Budget approximately $20–40 USD for souvenirs. Pack souvenirs carefully to avoid breakage. Confirm checkout time with Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange departure transport in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a peaceful walk, collect any shells or stones as free natural mementos, and say goodbye to the incredible Costa Rican landscape. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the resort if checkout is before your transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, either head directly to the airport via pre-booked shared shuttle, or use remaining time to explore a final local attraction near the airport (San José's Mercado Central is worth a visit if time permits — free entry, vibrant atmosphere, and excellent cheap food). Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at least 3 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of wildlife encounters, adrenaline adventures, and authentic cultural experiences. Reflect on the 13-day journey through one of the world's most biodiverse and beautiful countries.

meals.breakfast: Final Costa Rican breakfast — gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh tropical fruit one last time at a local soda near the resort. Budget $4–6 USD. Savor every bite!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or near the airport if time allows. San José's Mercado Central offers authentic and affordable meals for $4–6 USD. Airport food is significantly more expensive ($12–18 USD) — eat before security if possible.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or upon arrival at home destination.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details the night before. Allow extra time for the drive to San José airport — February traffic can be unpredictable. Declare any food items (coffee, chocolate) at customs in your home country. Keep receipts for any significant purchases. Consider writing a TripAdvisor review for local operators who provided exceptional budget-friendly experiences — it helps other travelers and supports local businesses. ¡Pura Vida!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room. Brief orientation of resort amenities.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Late-night snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night. Keep first night light — no activities scheduled. Confirm check-in details with resort ahead of time. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront to acclimate to the tropical climate and surroundings. Explore the resort grounds, pool area, and nearby beach stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local nature reserve or beach estuary for a self-guided introductory wildlife walk. Look for howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas in the coastal vegetation. Stop at a local surf shop or visitor center to gather maps and tips for the coming days.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beach. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range beachside restaurant near the resort. Relax and prepare for the adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort (included or ~$12–$18)
meals.lunch: Casual soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort – try a casado (rice, beans, protein, salad) for ~$8–$12
meals.dinner: Beachside seafood restaurant – fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and a local Imperial beer for ~$20–$30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from travel. Apply sunscreen and stay hydrated — the tropical sun is intense even in February. Pick up any missing gear (insect repellent, water shoes) at a local store.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Tortuguero National Park (arrange travel via domestic flight or shuttle + boat combo from San José area, ~3–4 hours). Board a guided wildlife boat safari through the jungle canals of Tortuguero. Spot caimans, river turtles, howler and spider monkeys, sloths, and an abundance of tropical birds from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tortuguero village. Explore the small, car-free village on foot. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about the park's famous nesting sea turtles and broader conservation efforts. Optional short hike on a jungle trail within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a local lodge restaurant in Tortuguero village. Overnight stay at a mid-range eco-lodge in Tortuguero (e.g., Manatus Hotel or similar ~$80–$120/night) for proximity to the park.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Box lunch provided by tour operator on the boat or a small local soda in Tortuguero village (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Lodge or village restaurant in Tortuguero – Caribbean-style rice and beans (gallo pinto), plantains, and fresh fish (~$18–$25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero requires overnight stay due to distance. Book the Tortuguero Wildlife Boat Safari experience in advance. Bring rain gear — the Caribbean side of Costa Rica receives frequent rainfall. February is a drier month overall but always be prepared. Mosquito repellent is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Optional early-morning bird watching walk along Tortuguero's jungle trails with a local guide. The dawn chorus in Tortuguero is extraordinary — look for toucans, herons, kingfishers, and parrots. Return to lodge for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat back to the mainland and arrange transport toward the Arenal Volcano region (La Fortuna area, ~3–4 hours by shuttle). Check into a mid-range lodge near Arenal (e.g., Arenal Manoa Hotel or similar, ~$70–$100/night). Freshen up and take in the dramatic views of Arenal Volcano.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous Arenal hot springs. Several mid-range options exist such as Baldi Hot Springs or Tabacón area pools (~$30–$50 entry). Dinner at a La Fortuna restaurant with volcano views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Tortuguero eco-lodge (included with stay)
meals.lunch: Roadside soda during transit or packed snacks (~$8–$10)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in La Fortuna – try La Cantina or Don Rufino for mid-range Costa Rican cuisine (~$20–$30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tortuguero to Arenal transfer is scenic but long. Book a shuttle in advance for comfort. Confirm hot springs entry fees and hours before visiting. Arenal Volcano is one of Costa Rica's most iconic landmarks.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike. Begin in the morning with a guided walk across a network of suspension bridges high above the rainforest floor near Arenal. Spot sloths, toucans, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys from elevated vantage points. Guides explain the rainforest ecosystem in detail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hanging bridges circuit or take a separate guided rainforest hike along the base of Arenal Volcano. Visit the Arenal Volcano National Park lava fields trail for dramatic geological scenery and panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna. Explore the town's vibrant main street. Visit the La Fortuna Waterfall if time permits (short hike, ~$20 entry). Dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Arenal lodge (included)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by hanging bridges tour operator or a soda near the park entrance (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Lava Lounge or Kappa Restaurant in La Fortuna – burgers, pasta, and local dishes in a relaxed atmosphere (~$18–$28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Arenal Hanging Bridges tour in advance. Wear sturdy hiking shoes and bring a light rain jacket. The hanging bridges tour typically takes 3–4 hours. Start early to avoid midday heat and afternoon rain showers.

day_by_day.morning: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal — one of Costa Rica's largest lakes with stunning volcano backdrops. Rent equipment through a local outfitter (~$25–$40). Look for birds along the lake's forested shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Arenal Eco Zoo or a local butterfly and reptile garden for up-close wildlife encounters including frogs, snakes, and insects. Alternatively, take a guided horseback riding tour through the Arenal countryside (~$45–$65 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in La Fortuna. Enjoy a sunset dinner with volcano views. Prepare luggage for the next day's travel to Monteverde.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at lodge in La Fortuna
meals.lunch: Casual café in La Fortuna town center – sandwiches, fresh fruit, and natural fruit juices (~$10–$15)
meals.dinner: El Novillo del Arenal steakhouse or similar – grilled meats and local sides with volcano views (~$22–$32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Arenal is best in the morning before winds pick up. Horseback riding requires advance booking. Pack and organize bags the night before for an early Monteverde departure.

day_by_day.morning: Depart La Fortuna for Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3–4 hours by shuttle or the scenic jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal). Arrive in Santa Elena/Monteverde and check into a mid-range cloud forest lodge (e.g., Arco Iris Lodge or El Establo Mountain Hotel, ~$70–$110/night). Enjoy the cool, misty cloud forest climate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden or the Orchid Garden for a gentle introductory wildlife experience. Walk the Santa Elena town to browse local artisan shops, coffee cooperatives, and chocolate tours. Sample locally produced cloud forest coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an optional night walk in the cloud forest with a naturalist guide (~$25–$35). Spot nocturnal wildlife including tree frogs, stick insects, and sleeping birds. Dinner in Santa Elena.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Arenal lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda during transit or arrive and eat in Santa Elena (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Morpho's Restaurant or Sofia Restaurant in Santa Elena – creative Costa Rican fusion cuisine (~$20–$30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal is a unique and scenic experience — highly recommended over the road route. Monteverde is significantly cooler than the lowlands — pack a light fleece or jacket. Night walks must be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: HEADLINE EXPERIENCE: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. Experience multiple platforms, Tarzan swings, and suspended bridges high above the forest floor. Operators such as Original Canopy Tour or 100% Aventura offer thrilling multi-line circuits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a guided hike through primary cloud forest. Walk misty trails in search of the resplendent quetzal (February is a good month for quetzal sightings), bellbirds, and rare orchids. A certified naturalist guide greatly enhances wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory (La Lechería) for a tasting of locally produced artisan cheeses — a unique local tradition. Relax over dinner and review photos from the day's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Monteverde lodge
meals.lunch: Café at the cloud forest reserve entrance or packed lunch (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Trio Restaurant or El Jardín at Santa Elena – wood-fired dishes and local specialties (~$20–$28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line canopy tour and cloud forest reserve guided hike in advance — both are very popular and fill up quickly. Wear closed-toe shoes and secure any loose items before zip-lining. The cloud forest can be wet and muddy — waterproof boots are ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Children's Eternal Rainforest (Bosque Eterno de los Niños) — the largest private reserve in Costa Rica. Join a guided morning hike through pristine rainforest with excellent wildlife viewing opportunities. Look for peccaries, coatis, and a remarkable diversity of birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde for Manuel Antonio on the Pacific coast (approximately 4–5 hours by shuttle). Arrive at the coast and check into a mid-range hotel near Manuel Antonio (e.g., Hotel Costa Verde or Arenas del Mar, ~$80–$130/night). Unwind with a late-afternoon beach swim.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your first Pacific sunset of the trip from the beach. Dinner at a restaurant in Quepos or along the Manuel Antonio road.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Monteverde lodge
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or roadside soda during transit (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: El Avión Restaurant in Manuel Antonio (housed in a retired military plane) – seafood and grilled meats with ocean views (~$25–$35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde to Manuel Antonio shuttle is a long travel day — start early. Book shuttle in advance. Confirm hotel check-in time and request early check-in if arriving before standard time. Manuel Antonio is one of Costa Rica's most visited destinations — book all activities in advance.

day_by_day.morning: HEADLINE EXPERIENCE: Manuel Antonio National Park Wildlife & Beach Day. Enter the park early (opens at 7:00 AM — arrive by 7:30 AM to beat crowds). Join a certified park guide for a 2–3 hour wildlife walk through the rainforest trails. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, squirrel monkeys, sloths, iguanas, and colorful birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on one of Manuel Antonio's stunning beaches within the park (Playa Manuel Antonio or Playa Espadilla Sur). Swim in the calm turquoise waters, snorkel near the rocky outcrops, or simply relax under a palm tree. Picnic lunch on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel and freshen up. Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Pacific. Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Quepos.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before park opening
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from hotel or purchased at park entrance kiosks (~$10–$15)
meals.dinner: La Cantina or Gabriella's in Quepos – fresh seafood, ceviche, and tropical cocktails (~$20–$28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap — book entry tickets online in advance at sinac.go.cr. Hiring a park guide at the entrance (~$25–$35) dramatically improves wildlife spotting. Do NOT feed the monkeys — it is harmful and prohibited. Store valuables securely as monkeys are notorious thieves.

day_by_day.morning: Sea kayaking or snorkeling tour from Manuel Antonio's coast. Paddle around the rocky marine outcrops and explore sea caves along the coastline. Spot pelicans, frigatebirds, and marine life including tropical fish and sea turtles. Tours depart from Playa Biesanz (~$45–$65 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rainmaker Conservation Project near Quepos for a private hanging bridges and waterfall hike through secondary rainforest. Alternatively, take a dolphin and whale watching boat tour from Quepos marina (humpback whales and dolphins are commonly sighted in February off the Manuel Antonio coast, ~$65–$85 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Manuel Antonio. Enjoy a special mid-range splurge dinner at a restaurant with panoramic ocean views. Pack bags for tomorrow's travel to the Osa Peninsula.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel in Manuel Antonio
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche and patacones at a beachside soda in Quepos (~$10–$15)
meals.dinner: Kapi Kapi Restaurant or Barba Roja in Manuel Antonio – elevated Costa Rican cuisine with ocean views (~$28–$40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin and whale watching tours should be booked in advance. February is an excellent month for marine wildlife off the Pacific coast. Rainmaker Conservation Project requires advance booking. Begin packing for the Osa Peninsula — a more remote and rugged destination.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Manuel Antonio early for the Osa Peninsula (approximately 4–5 hours by shuttle to Puerto Jiménez or via domestic flight from Quepos to Puerto Jiménez, ~45 minutes). Check into a mid-range eco-lodge near Puerto Jiménez (e.g., Iguana Lodge or Bosque del Cabo, ~$90–$140/night). Brief orientation and gear check for tomorrow's Corcovado trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: HEADLINE EXPERIENCE: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek (Day 1 of 2). Enter Corcovado via the La Leona or San Pedrillo ranger station with a certified SINAC guide (mandatory for Corcovado). Trek through pristine primary rainforest — one of the most biodiverse places on Earth. Spot tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, anteaters, and an extraordinary diversity of jungle life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to eco-lodge. Debrief with your guide over dinner. Rest and recover for another full day in the jungle tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Manuel Antonio hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from eco-lodge or purchased in Puerto Jiménez (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at eco-lodge restaurant – fresh local ingredients, farm-to-table style (~$20–$30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado National Park requires advance permits and a certified guide — book at least 2–3 months in advance through the SINAC system or a reputable tour operator. A domestic flight from Quepos to Puerto Jiménez is strongly recommended to save travel time. Bring high-quality insect repellent, waterproof boots, and a dry bag for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Day 2 in Corcovado: Early morning jungle trek with your guide focusing on deeper primary forest trails. The dawn hours offer the best wildlife activity — look for harpy eagles, jaguars (rare but possible), giant anteaters, and river otters along jungle streams. Wade through river crossings and explore pristine beach stretches within the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Corcovado and transfer back toward the main resort (Aegean Bliss Resort) via domestic flight or shuttle. Arrive at the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxing swim in the ocean or pool. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days across Costa Rica's most iconic ecosystems.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at the best restaurant at or near Aegean Bliss Resort. Toast to an incredible eco-adventure journey through cloud forests, volcanoes, jungle canals, Pacific beaches, and one of the world's most biodiverse rainforests.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Osa eco-lodge before final Corcovado morning
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail or at the ranger station (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's restaurant or a top-rated nearby restaurant – splurge slightly for the final night (~$30–$45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer from Osa Peninsula to the resort well in advance — logistics in the Osa can be complex. If flying out of Costa Rica on Day 14, confirm that the resort is within reasonable distance of Juan Santamaría Airport and book an early morning transfer. Corcovado is the crown jewel of Costa Rican biodiversity — a truly once-in-a-lifetime experience to end the trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Walk among the treetops on a network of hanging bridges suspended above the rainforest floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided or guided eco-walk offers incredible biodiversity including morpho butterflies, coatis, and resplendent quetzals, with stunning volcano views on clear days.
experiences.location: La Fortuna, Arenal Volcano National Park

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Wildlife & Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most beloved national park where lush rainforest meets pristine Pacific beaches. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, and scarlet macaws on well-marked trails before relaxing on the stunning Playa Manuel Antonio. A certified naturalist guide maximizes wildlife encounters.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biodiverse places on a guided trek through Corcovado's primary rainforest. Encounter tapirs, peccaries, scarlet macaws, and if lucky, the elusive jaguar. This raw, off-the-beaten-path experience is the pinnacle of eco-adventure in Central America.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront property. Welcome amenities, champagne turn-down service, and a late-night light snack await in your suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter of local cheeses, tropical fruits, charcuterie, and sparkling wine prepared by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with a luxury ground service (e.g., Viajes Mundiales or a resort-coordinated chauffeur). Confirm resort reception is available 24/7. Unpack and rest — a full adventure begins tomorrow. Ensure passports and travel documents are ready for customs.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort orientation. Take a private guided walk of the resort's beachfront gardens and coastal trails with a resident naturalist who introduces you to local bird species, coastal flora, and the rhythms of Costa Rican beach life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the luxury of the Aegean Bliss Resort — spend the afternoon at the infinity pool overlooking the Pacific, enjoy a signature spa treatment (volcanic stone massage or rainforest botanical wrap), and explore the resort's private beach stretch at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring Costa Rican-inspired dishes: ceviche with tiger's milk, grilled corvina with plantain purée, and a local chocolate lava cake paired with premium Costa Rican coffee.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast buffet at the resort featuring tropical fruits, freshly baked pastries, made-to-order eggs, and local Guanacaste cheeses with freshly brewed Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside light lunch at the resort's poolside bar — grilled lobster tacos, avocado salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. $120–$160 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate recovery and orientation day after the late arrival. Use this day to adjust to the time zone, hydrate, and prepare gear for upcoming adventures. Book any remaining excursion confirmations with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private guided Manuel Antonio National Park Wildlife & Beach Day excursion. Arrive early (park opens at 7:00 AM) to maximize wildlife sightings before midday heat. Your expert naturalist guide leads you through lush rainforest trails where you'll spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and coatimundis with a high-powered spotting scope and binoculars provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the rainforest loop, descend to the park's pristine Playa Manuel Antonio — a crescent of white sand framed by jungle. Enjoy a private catered beach picnic lunch, then snorkel in the calm turquoise waters or simply relax on the beach. Spot more wildlife including raccoons and ghost crabs along the shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and head to a highly-rated local fine-dining restaurant near Quepos/Manuel Antonio — La Luna at Gaia Hotel is an excellent choice with panoramic ocean views, serving elevated Costa Rican cuisine with a farm-to-table philosophy.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before 6:30 AM departure — eggs Benedict, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Private catered picnic basket at Playa Manuel Antonio — artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit salad, sparkling water, and local craft beer
meals.dinner: La Luna Restaurant at Gaia Hotel & Reserve — try the seared mahi-mahi with passion fruit reduction and yuca gratin (approx. $80–$120 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitor numbers — ensure tickets are pre-booked well in advance. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only (required inside the park). Bring waterproof sandals, light breathable clothing, and insect repellent. The park closes at 4:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs early for Arenal Volcano region (approx. 3–3.5 hour scenic drive through Costa Rica's central highlands). Upon arrival, check into your pre-arranged luxury lodge near Arenal (e.g., Nayara Springs or The Springs Resort & Spa) for a 2-night stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike — walk among the treetops on a network of suspended hanging bridges above the rainforest floor with a private expert naturalist guide. Spot poison dart frogs, toucans, howler monkeys, and spectacular views of Arenal Volcano. The 3-km loop offers breathtaking perspectives of the surrounding cloud forest ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in natural volcanic hot springs at your luxury lodge's private thermal pools as dusk settles over the volcano. Enjoy cocktails poolside, then dine at the lodge's restaurant featuring locally sourced ingredients, fresh heart of palm salad, and slow-braised beef tenderloin.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — grab-and-go option if needed
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic roadside restaurant en route to Arenal — try traditional casado (rice, beans, plantains, and protein) at a quality local establishment
meals.dinner: Romantic dinner at Nayara Springs' Amor Loco restaurant or The Springs' Las Ventanas — volcanic stone-grilled meats, local vegetables, and artisan desserts (approx. $90–$130 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Arenal is scenic — request your driver to stop at a viewpoint near Lake Arenal for photos. Pack a light rain jacket as the Arenal region receives frequent afternoon showers. The hanging bridges are accessible to most fitness levels with moderate walking involved.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private guided birdwatching and wildlife walk around the Arenal Lake and surrounding forest reserve. With a specialist birding guide, seek out resplendent quetzals (possible in higher elevations), toucans, kingfishers, and herons along the lakeshore. This is one of Costa Rica's premier birding circuits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on the glassy waters of Lake Arenal with Arenal Volcano as your dramatic backdrop. Follow with a private chocolate and coffee plantation tour at a nearby organic farm — learn the bean-to-bar process and participate in a guided tasting of single-origin Costa Rican cacao and micro-lot coffees.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge terrace with unobstructed volcano views, followed by a private in-villa dinner experience — your lodge's chef prepares a personalized 4-course Costa Rican fusion menu in the privacy of your suite or villa.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the lodge — avocado toast with local cheese, tropical fruit plate, freshly squeezed juices, and premium Costa Rican pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the chocolate farm or a nearby lakeside restaurant — fresh salads, local fish, and handcrafted cacao beverages
meals.dinner: Private in-villa chef dinner experience — 4-course personalized menu with local wine and spirits pairing (approx. $150–$200 USD per person, arranged through concierge)

day_by_day.notes: Book the in-villa private dinner experience at least 24 hours in advance through your lodge concierge. The morning birdwatching walk should begin no later than 5:30–6:00 AM for optimal wildlife activity. Bring a light layer as early mornings near Arenal can be cool and misty.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal and transfer north toward the Tortuguero region (approx. 3–4 hours including a boat segment). The journey itself is an adventure — your private transfer includes a scenic drive to the embarkation point, followed by a motorized canoe ride through jungle waterways to reach Tortuguero. Check into a premium jungle lodge (e.g., Tortuga Lodge by Costa Rica Expeditions).
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide through the park's legendary network of jungle canals on a private guided boat safari. Spot caimans basking on riverbanks, river otters playing in the current, three-toed sloths hanging in cecropia trees, great green macaws, and dozens of waterbird species including herons and anhingas.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset river cruise along the main Tortuguero canal with champagne and canapés served aboard your private boat. Watch as the jungle symphony crescendos at dusk — howler monkeys roar, toucans return to roost, and the sky turns amber over the Caribbean horizon. Dinner at the lodge's open-air restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Arenal lodge before departure — eggs any style, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Tortuguero lodge upon arrival — Caribbean-style rice and beans (gallo pinto), fresh fish, and tropical juice
meals.dinner: Tortuga Lodge open-air dining — Caribbean-influenced cuisine featuring coconut curry shrimp, plantain-crusted snapper, and rum-infused desserts (approx. $70–$100 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small aircraft — no roads connect to the village. Pack light for this segment as luggage is transported by canoe. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and electronics. Insect repellent is essential in this rainforest region. February is a good time for wildlife but rain is possible.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn sea turtle nesting site visit (if February timing aligns with leatherback nesting season — February marks the beginning of leatherback season at Tortuguero). A certified guide leads a small group to the black sand beach to observe nesting or hatching turtles under strict conservation protocols. This is one of the most moving wildlife encounters on earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Second Tortuguero canal boat safari focusing on deeper, less-visited waterways — explore channels where caimans, Jesus Christ lizards, and freshwater turtles are commonly seen. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about decades of conservation research protecting Tortuguero's legendary turtle populations.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class with the lodge's chef — learn to prepare traditional Caribbean Costa Rican dishes including rondon (seafood coconut stew), patacones, and tres leches cake. Enjoy the meal you've prepared as your dinner with paired local craft beers and tropical cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before pre-dawn turtle walk — fruit, granola, and coffee provided by lodge
meals.lunch: Lodge lunch featuring fresh Caribbean fare — lobster soup, coconut rice, and fresh tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Your own creation from the cooking class, enjoyed in the lodge's dining area — Caribbean seafood stew, fried plantains, and tres leches cake (included in cooking class experience)

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle encounters are strictly regulated — no flash photography, red-light torches only, and you must remain with a certified guide at all times. Confirm turtle activity with your lodge naturalist the evening before as sightings depend on nesting cycles. The cooking class should be booked through the lodge concierge upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tortuguero — early kayaking through the narrow jungle creeks bordering the national park, paddling silently to maximize wildlife encounters. Your guide points out sleeping bats in hollow trees, camouflaged basilisk lizards, and rare waterbirds in the still morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat transfer back to the mainland, followed by a scenic luxury vehicle transfer toward Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approx. 4–5 hours). Arrive at your premium cloud forest lodge (e.g., Monteverde Lodge & Gardens or El Silencio Lodge & Spa) and check in for a 2-night stay.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night walk in the cloud forest surrounding your lodge — with headlamps and a specialist naturalist guide, discover the nocturnal world of Monteverde: glass frogs, red-eyed tree frogs, kinkajous, sleeping hummingbirds, and the eerie calls of owls and nightjars echoing through the mist.

meals.breakfast: Final Caribbean breakfast at Tortuga Lodge — gallo pinto, eggs, fresh mango, and strong Costa Rican coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch stop en route to Monteverde at a quality roadside restaurant in Liberia or Cañas — traditional Costa Rican casado or grilled meats
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Monteverde lodge restaurant — highland cuisine featuring mushroom risotto with local fungi, beef tenderloin, and cloud forest honey dessert (approx. $80–$110 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde includes a famous unpaved section — ensure your private transfer uses a 4WD vehicle. The journey is long but the scenery is spectacular. The night walk typically begins at 7:30–8:00 PM and lasts 1.5–2 hours. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — the headline adventure of the trip. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits with up to 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and rappelling sections. Your professional guides ensure top-tier safety while you experience the forest from a thrilling aerial perspective, gliding above the treetops with panoramic views of the Gulf of Nicoya.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve with a private expert naturalist. Seek out the legendary resplendent quetzal — February is within the quetzal breeding season making sightings more likely. Also watch for bellbirds, emerald toucanets, and the incredible biodiversity of this UNESCO-recognized ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Visit to a local artisan cheese dairy and coffee cooperative for a premium tasting experience — Monteverde is famous for its high-altitude dairy traditions brought by Quaker settlers. Then enjoy a candlelit dinner at a top Monteverde restaurant such as Sofia Restaurant, known for its creative nuevo Latino cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the cloud forest lodge — cloud forest mushroom omelette, local cheese plate, fresh-pressed orange juice, and pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at the tour operator's lodge or a nearby restaurant — hearty sandwiches, local soups, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Sofia Restaurant, Monteverde — nuevo Latino tasting menu featuring plantain-crusted chicken, hearts of palm ceviche, and passion fruit crème brûlée (approx. $70–$100 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Zip-line tours require participants to meet weight limits (typically 100kg/220lbs maximum) and wear closed-toe shoes. The cloud forest reserve has limited daily visitor capacity — pre-book your private guided walk. Morning hours offer the best quetzal sighting opportunities, so consider reversing the afternoon and morning activities if quetzal sightings are a top priority.

day_by_day.morning: Final Monteverde morning — private horseback riding through cloud forest trails and highland pastures with sweeping views of the Nicoya Peninsula and Pacific Ocean on clear days. Your guide narrates the history of the Monteverde region, its Quaker heritage, and conservation legacy as you ride through mist-draped landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde and transfer south toward the Osa Peninsula / Corcovado region (approx. 5–6 hours, or consider a private charter flight from Quepos or Palmar Sur for a premium time-saving option). Check into a luxury eco-lodge near Corcovado (e.g., Lapa Rios Lodge or Playa Cativo Lodge).
day_by_day.evening: Arrival and orientation at your Osa Peninsula eco-lodge. Enjoy a welcome cocktail on the jungle-view terrace as the symphony of howler monkeys and scarlet macaws fills the forest around you. Early dinner at the lodge to rest before tomorrow's major expedition.

meals.breakfast: Final cloud forest breakfast at Monteverde lodge — full gourmet spread before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch en route or at the charter flight terminal — packed gourmet lunch box arranged by lodge, or a restaurant stop in Quepos
meals.dinner: Lapa Rios or Playa Cativo lodge restaurant — farm-to-jungle cuisine featuring Osa Peninsula seafood, local tropical fruits, and organic vegetables grown on-site (approx. $80–$120 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Strongly recommend booking a private charter flight (e.g., Nature Air or Sansa) from Quepos or San José to Puerto Jiménez or Drake Bay to avoid the long overland journey to the Osa Peninsula. Flight takes approximately 45 minutes versus 5–6 hours by road. This is a worthwhile luxury upgrade. Confirm lodge boat or ground transfer from the airstrip.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek — the crown jewel of Costa Rican wildlife experiences. Depart early by boat to reach the park's San Pedrillo or La Leona entrance. Your private certified guide leads you deep into primary rainforest that National Geographic has called 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, four species of monkeys, harpy eagles, and an astonishing density of plant and animal life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado trek through ancient primary forest, crossing rivers and navigating jungle trails to reach interior viewpoints. Spot scarlet macaws in flight, poison dart frogs on the forest floor, and perhaps a jaguar track — Corcovado hosts one of the last viable jaguar populations in Central America. Lunch is served in the jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Return by boat to the lodge in late afternoon. Enjoy a restorative massage at the lodge spa, followed by a special candlelit dinner on a private jungle terrace — a personalized dining experience arranged by the lodge with local seafood and organic produce.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-trek breakfast at the lodge — energy-rich foods: eggs, rice and beans, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed jungle lunch prepared by the lodge — artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, energy bars, and water (carried in your daypack)
meals.dinner: Private candlelit terrace dinner at the lodge — whole grilled snapper with chimichurri, roasted local vegetables, and a decadent dark chocolate mousse made with Osa cacao (approx. $100–$150 USD per person, arranged through concierge)

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado National Park requires an authorized guide — solo entry is not permitted. Wear long pants and long sleeves for jungle protection, waterproof hiking boots, and apply DEET-based insect repellent. Bring at least 2 liters of water per person. The trek is moderately strenuous — inform your guide of any fitness limitations. February conditions are generally good with manageable humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise dolphin and whale watching boat expedition off the Osa Peninsula — the waters of Drake Bay and the Golfo Dulce are among the most productive marine mammal habitats in the Pacific. Spot spinner dolphins, bottlenose dolphins, and possibly humpback whales (February is within the northern humpback season). Snorkel at Caño Island Biological Reserve, a premier snorkeling and diving destination with sea turtles, reef sharks, and vibrant coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a leisurely afternoon — final wildlife walks on the lodge's private reserve trails, hammock time on your jungle-view terrace, or an indulgent spa session. Take time to reflect on the extraordinary biodiversity witnessed throughout the trip. Pack and prepare for tomorrow's return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the lodge — the chef prepares a special multi-course celebration of Costa Rican flavors: fresh ceviche, whole roasted pargo (red snapper), local heart of palm salad, and a spectacular tropical fruit pavlova. Toast the journey with premium Costa Rican rum cocktails and local wines.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-boat breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and coffee before the marine expedition
meals.lunch: Post-snorkeling lunch aboard the boat or at the lodge upon return — fresh ceviche, grilled fish, coconut rice, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at the lodge — multi-course chef's special menu with cocktail pairing (approx. $130–$180 USD per person, pre-arranged with lodge)

day_by_day.notes: Caño Island snorkeling requires a park fee and must be arranged through a licensed operator — your lodge concierge will handle all logistics. Bring an underwater camera or GoPro for the marine excursion. Confirm airport transfer logistics and flight details for tomorrow's departure. Leave a gratuity for lodge staff who have made the stay exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise wildlife walk on the lodge's private reserve — a quiet, reflective last encounter with the Osa Peninsula's extraordinary nature. Listen for howler monkeys, watch scarlet macaws fly overhead, and say farewell to the jungle. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the lodge before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight or ground transfer from the Osa Peninsula back to San José Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO). Allow ample time for the journey — charter flight is approximately 45 minutes, ground transfer is 5–6 hours. Depending on your departing flight time, enjoy a final lunch in San José at a top restaurant such as La Esquina de Buenos Aires or Alma de Café in the Gran Hotel Costa Rica.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of cloud forests, jungle canals, volcanic landscapes, and the most biodiverse wildlife encounters on the planet. If your flight departs late evening, consider a lounge upgrade at SJO for a comfortable pre-flight experience.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the Osa lodge — a full spread celebrating 13 days of extraordinary Costa Rican hospitality: tropical fruits, local cheeses, freshly baked bread, eggs, and the finest Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch in San José — La Esquina de Buenos Aires for premium grilled meats, or Sikwa Restaurant for elevated indigenous Costa Rican cuisine (approx. $60–$90 USD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and ensure all departure taxes are accounted for (typically included in international airfare). Purchase last-minute Costa Rican souvenirs at the airport — single-origin coffee, artisan chocolates, and locally made crafts make excellent gifts. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — do not purchase anything made from wildlife products. Consider leaving a review for exceptional guides and lodges to support Costa Rica's ecotourism community.
